thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: Dedicated pool 'zenith-enterprise' (tenant: ZenithCorp) GPU utilization 100% across all nodes. Queue length spiking for requests routed to rtx_a100-1. Autoscaler did NOT provision more because pool is at hard cap. first_seen=2934567880

alice_oncall: acked. Paging @ben_sre and @carla_runtime. Are we seeing customer impact or just internal queueing?

ben_sre: looking. queue length = 420 reqs, avg latency 4.2s -> tail 18s, some 503s start showing at 2934568001. Logs show model=redwood-3b-8q running hot, per-tenant token rate jumped x6.

carla_runtime: confirm. The pool is pinned to a tenant max_gpus=16 (contract). Currently 16 in use. Autoscaler has burst_disabled for this pool per org policy. We can: 1) enable short-term burst override, 2) route to quantized fallback model, or 3) throttle tenant with grace. Which do we want?

alice_oncall: prefer non-throttling. What's fastest to reduce load?

carla_runtime: fastest is routing to smaller quantized model (redwood-3b-q4f) for non-SLA-critical routes + enable burst for 30m while we observe. I have a CLI snippet to toggle routing and burst.

carla_runtime: ```
# enable 30m burst for zenith-enterprise pool
rwctl pools burst set --pool zenith-enterprise --tenant ZenithCorp --gpus 8 --duration 30m --reason "emergency spillover"
# update routing rule to prefer quantized variant for non-critical routes
rwctl routing update --tenant ZenithCorp --rule "if route != /inference/priority then model=redwood-3b-q4f"
```

ben_sre: running checks, mounting metrics dashboard now. also starting a drain of low-priority queue items: `kubectl exec -n inference -c router router-01 -- /usr/local/bin/drain-tenant --tenant ZenithCorp --priority low`

incident-bot: Action queued: burst request submitted (request_id=burst-2934568122). Awaiting approver.

frank_vpeng: I can approve emergency burst. Approving now: `approved_by=frank_vpeng`

incident-bot: Burst approved and applied. Pool +8 GPUs (burst) started provisioning. Expected ready ~120s. request_id=burst-2934568122 status=provisioning :rocket:

david_cs: heads-up to @elaine_acct — ZenithCorp support line reporting increased 5xx for some users. Can we send a quick customer note? Keep it factual; say we're mitigating.

elaine_acct: drafting. Proposed msg: "We're seeing elevated inference latency for a subset of requests routed to your dedicated pool. We've applied temporary burst capacity and routing to a lower-cost model for non-priority requests. We'll monitor and follow up with a timeline." ok to send? :eyes:

alice_oncall: go ahead after we confirm burst is up and observed latency drops.

incident-bot: Burst nodes are ready. status=active at 2934568205. Pool effective GPUs = 24.

ben_sre: after burst + routing change: queue dropped from 420 -> 48 over 60s. p95 latency down to 1.1s. Error rate 503 -> 0.6%. Looks good.

carla_runtime: leaving routing change active for 20m, then we'll roll back slowly. I'll also set autoscaler_override to allow future short bursts for this tenant if quota bumped. TODO: follow-up PR for config.

frank_vpeng: long-term: account needs reserved bump or contract change. Ops team, prepare offer.

david_cs: Sent customer note at 2934568220. Elaine included mitigation steps and ETA to follow up.

elaine_acct: Customer reply (via support): "Thanks, please keep us updated. This affects our interactive product but not batch jobs." They asked for SLA impact assessment.

alice_oncall: recording timeline. tagging for postmortem. Immediate actions: 1) confirm rollback plan, 2) document why autoscaler blocked (policy), 3) customer follow-up. Can we annotate runbook with the new CLI steps?

carla_runtime: will open runbook PR with commands and a safer default: allow single emergency burst per 24h.

ben_sre: will collect logs and attach perf graphs. ETA 1h.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. incident_id=INC-2934567890. If error rate rises above 1% in next 15m, page again. :white_check_mark: 

alice_oncall: thanks team. staying on this for monitoring window. :thumbsup:
